pr_title: Consistently start the agent as root and rely on it to drop privileges properly.
pr_body:
##### Summary

This ensures that we consistently start the agent as root when running as a system service and properly trust it to drop privileges during startup (which it does in fact do correctly). It also updates the relevant scripts to trust the agent to create required directories itself, as starting as root lets it do so properly.

This also tidies up handling of the preparation of required directories during startup, and adds our log directory to the list of directories we attempt to create if it does not exist.

##### Test Plan

Testing requires installing the agent from this PR on a variety of different systems and confirming that it starts up correctly.

##### Additional Information

Fixes: https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/9701, plus a bunch of other issues we keep seeing intermittently regarding handling of require directories on startup.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Systemd service file should properly honor what user Netdata is configured to run as.
issue_context.body:
Currently, the systemd unit files we install blindly assume that the Netdata user and group names are `netdata`. While this works for the common case, it fails horribly in two cases:

* The user has installed with different username for the `netdata` user.
* The user has configured Netdata to run as a different user than the `netdata` user.

A reliable solution to this is non-trivial, and probably involves having Netdata itself handle switching to the user it's supposed to run as instead of having systemd do so prior to running Netdata.
comments:
> The user has installed with different username for the netdata user.
> The user has configured Netdata to run as a different user than the netdata user.

Can we just simply not allow this in the first place? cc @amoss -- I find allowing "to much" flexibility to be problematic here honestly. It unnecessarily complicates what we have to support and the packaging/ci and testing code/infra we have to write and maintain.
I also wouldn't call this a "bug" per se so have categorised as an "enhancement". Its really a missing feature of how we package/ship the SystemD Unit.

No, this is a bug, we currently support both of these configurations, but do not work correctly in either of them without further user intervention.

Just having Netdata be responsible itself for dropping to the correct user account, always starting it as root, and then making it create the directories it needs if they aren't there (like it should be doing anyway) should fix this, it's just not something we can trivially fix with packaging changes.
I agree that it is a bug - if we support the option to change the username then we have to support it everywhere.

@cpipilas, @stelfrag this one has been around for a long time and will probably need some changes in the agent code itself to actually fix properly (see the second paragraph of https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/9701#issuecomment-673474511 for info), but it would be nice if we could properly get this groomed and prioritized properly in the backlog.
@Ferroin It's a bug and needs to be fixed. Let's add it in our backlog for proper grooming/sizing since to my understanding we are talking about horizontal changes in the agent.

On further inspection, this doesn’t appear to need any changes to the agent code to be fixed, but the relevant agent code could use a bit of cleanup for sanity reasons so I’ll take care of that at the same time.
